raw_response:
My land here in Quzhou has always been wheat-corn land. My mother grew wheat and corn, I grew wheat and corn, and that's what I'll grow this year too. I have about 5 mu. I can't do much else at my age — my back is not so good anymore, and my husband passed some years ago.

In the autumn I plant wheat. Always winter wheat. It goes in October after the rains slow down. I buy the seeds from the village supply station — they sell the approved kind now, not the old seeds we used to save. I use the compound fertilizer they sell at the market, plus some extra urea when the wheat is coming up in spring. I flood the field a few times from the canal — before the ground freezes, then again in spring when it starts growing again, then when the ears are forming.

After I harvest the wheat in June, I plant corn right away in the same field. I don't plow — no point, and I can't do that much work alone. My son helps me sometimes. The corn goes in fast with a small machine the village rents out. I put fertilizer down then top-dress again when it's knee-high. It needs water in July and August when it's hottest and driest.

I don't take chances with new crops or methods. I do what I know. The government gives subsidies for fertilizer and seed, so I use what they suggest. I don't change things.
